subject: chemistry
title: Chemical Changes Adventure 2 · Neutralisation & Salts
welcome_lead: Mix and match: acid + base, acid + carbonate, acid + metal — and name the salts.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry neutralisation reactions, salt naming and the three acid + base/metal/carbonate patterns.
final_note: You can predict the products of acid reactions and name the salt every time.

concepts.def: Acid + base reaction making salt and water
Ionic compound from an acid where H⁺ is replaced
HCl → chloride; H₂SO₄ → sulfate; HNO₃ → nitrate

walkthroughs.body_html:
Acids react three classic ways:

1. Acid + base → salt + water
2. Acid + metal carbonate → salt + water + CO₂
3. Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen

Carbonates fizz (CO₂). Metals fizz too (H₂) — test it with a squeaky pop.

The acid decides the salt's surname:

HCl → chloride
H₂SO₄ → sulfate
HNO₃ → nitrate

The metal (or base's metal) is the first name. Example: NaOH + HCl → sodium chloride + water.

Acid + base: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. Salt = sodium sulfate.

Acid + carbonate: 2HCl + CaCO₃ → CaCl₂ + H₂O + CO₂. Salt = calcium chloride.

Acid + metal: Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂. Salt = magnesium chloride.
